description: Over-grouping trap: two same-type crash-loop alerts in the same namespace look like one platform-wide problem, but the logs show unrelated root causes (a memory leak vs a config error). Correct grouping = TWO separate incidents. Anti-hallucination codes OOM-INV-3391 and CONFIG-ERR-7742 are discoverable only in logs.

alerts.title: Pod inventory-worker is crash looping
alerts.description: Pod backends/inventory-worker-6c47b9d8f5-h2ltq (container worker) has restarted 6 times in the last 20 minutes.

alerts.title: Pod notification-worker is crash looping
alerts.description: Pod backends/notification-worker-59f8c6b7d4-k9xmp (container worker) has restarted 7 times in the last 20 minutes.

expected_output: Must create TWO separate incidents — one for b1-inventory-crashloop and one for b2-notification-crashloop. They must NOT be placed in the same incident.
Must have investigated before deciding: called the evidence tools (get_pod_logs and/or kubectl_describe / get_resource_events) for BOTH inventory-worker and notification-worker.
Must identify that inventory-worker's crash loop is caused by an out-of-memory condition / memory leak (OOMKilled, exit 137), distinct from notification-worker's cause.
Must identify that notification-worker's crash loop is caused by a configuration error — the missing required environment variable SMTP_RELAY_URL (CONFIG-ERR-7742), not memory.
Must provide grouping_reasoning for each alert.
